authority: experiment-owner direction to continue evaluating OpenCode tools

finding.cause: The OpenCode workflow adapter has no 'repowise' treatment. The runner's preflight invokes the adapter with --treatment repowise, argparse rejects it against its choices list, and the process exits 2.
finding.evidence: tool_preflight_exit_code 2 with failure reason 'RepoWise ... preflight exited 2'. scripts/opencode_workflow_adapter.py TREATMENT_PROFILES contains eighteen treatments and repowise is not among them; mcp_list_exit_code was 0, so nothing else in the chain objected.
finding.why_this_is_a_protection_rather_than_a_b: The adapter branch is what writes the product's MCP registration into the lane-active opencode.json. Without it the model would receive no RepoWise surface at all while the run otherwise proceeded, which is the phantom-null shape that invalidated the first LeanCTX lanes. The argparse rejection stops that before any provider spend.

spend.note: Zero-spend. The failure occurred in the provider-free prepare phase; no lane reached the provider boundary.

required_before_this_profile_can_run: Implement a repowise branch in _runtime_env that registers the product's MCP server in the lane-active OpenCode configuration, matching the surfaces the profile declares.

The integration shape must come from RepoWise's own documented OpenCode support rather than being inferred from how other products are wired here. Guessing it would install an evaluator-authored integration, which the faithful-installation rule forbids and which would produce a result describing this repository rather than the product.

related.runner_side_is_defined: TOOL_CONFIGS['repowise-opencode-product-v2'] already specifies a lane-local uv venv installed from the pinned releases/repowise-0.45.0 tree, so only the adapter half is missing.
related.stale_label_noted: That entry's display_name reads 'RepoWise 0.39.0' while it installs 0.45.0. Cosmetic, and the same class as the version metadata corrected on 2026-09-21.

remaining_arm_readiness.retrieval-sdl-mcp-opencode-product-v1: adapter supports treatment sdl-mcp, but SDL_MCP_ROOT does not exist and has no pinned release candidate on disk, so it needs a pin before it can run
